title: CR functions at CR singularities approximation, extension, and hulls

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof of Theorem 2.3(ii), which claims 'There exists a real-analytic submanifold M such that, for every k, CR^k(M) ⊋ CR_P^k(M)', cites 'See Theorem 5.1 or Theorem 8.1.' However, earlier in Section 2 the paper states the identical claim ('there exist M for which the conclusion of the Baouendi–Trèves theorem does not hold even for CR_P functions') and cites 'See Theorem 5.1 or Theorem 9.1' instead. Moreover, the abstract and introduction describe Section 8 as containing the example w = z̄₁z₂, which is used to demonstrate the *positive* strong iterated SADH condition (a positive extension result), not a failure of CR^k = CR_P^k. The reference to 'Theorem 8.1' in the proof of 2.3(ii) is therefore inconsistent with the paper's own description of what Section 8 establishes, and inconsistent with the parallel citation to 'Theorem 9.1' used elsewhere for the same claim.

The example begins 'Given a compact set X, the set DH(X) need not be compact,' and then defines X = {z ∈ C³ : z₁ ∈ ∂D, z₂ = φ_k(z₁), z₃ = 1/k, k ∈ N} (Eq. 5). As literally written, this set is a countable union of disjoint circles with z₃ = 1/k, k ∈ N, which accumulate at z₃ = 0 but do not include any point with z₃ = 0. Such a set is not closed, hence not compact, contradicting the premise that X is compact. Yet later in the same example the text analyzes 'Ψ(ζ) = (α(ζ), β(ζ), 0)...an analytic disc [attached to X]', treating z₃ = 0 points as though they belong to X (or its closure), which is inconsistent with the stated formula for X that never attains z₃ = 0.

The example describes M given by Im w = |z₁|⁴ − |z₂|⁴ as 'a hypersurface with indefinite Levi form.' However, the Levi form is classically defined via the quadratic (second-order) terms of the defining function; since the defining equation here has no quadratic terms (only quartic terms), the actual Levi form at the origin is identically zero (degenerate/flat), not indefinite. Describing this quartic model as having an 'indefinite Levi form' misuses standard terminology, since the relevant indefinite object is the quartic form, not the Levi form, which is actually trivial (zero) at this CR singular point.
